merge.title: Display/button-net RC-decay self-check in the secure world against a factory OTP baseline, gated on a bench go/no-go study; input-current sense as an optional EVT-spin add-on
merge.threat:
A hardware add-on fitted between factory and buyer (reseller stage) or later (evil maid): a logger soldered to the NV3007 SPI nets (PA4 CS, PA5 SCK, PA7 MOSI, PB0 DC) or the two button nets (PA0/PA1), capturing seed words and PIN while the firmware is byte-for-byte genuine. This is the Ledger Nano X implant class (passive SPI sniff, glyph template match, LTE exfiltration). pq1 measures nothing electrical today; docs/security/user-device-verification.md:163-168 lists it as an accepted residual covered only by packaging, photos and SE genuine-check.

Honest answer to "can the FSBL or firmware detect malicious hardware": partly, and unproven. Firmware can plausibly detect a cheap soldered add-on load on a bus it drives. It cannot detect a buffered or non-contact tap, a board or panel swap, or an implant that also defeats the measurement. There is no peer-reviewed support for an on-device runtime detector of a high-impedance passive tap, and no wallet vendor ships one.
merge.proposal:
Three phases; only Phase 0 is recommended now.

PHASE 0 — bench go/no-go study (firmware only, prodtest image, no refusal path). This is BOOT-10's sound core, with its TSC and PDN legs removed.
- Method: per net, panel powered, CS high, no frame in flight, mask PWM paused. Configure the pad as a digital open-drain output with internal pull-up (not analog mode: the #705 IDR lesson, secure/src/hw/lcd_nv3007.rs:277-291). Drive low, release, time the Schmitt crossing. Measure the fall through the pull-down as well, to cancel threshold drift.
- Reference: the NC pad PA6 gives tau_ref = R_pu x C_pad, so each net is reported as C_net = C_pad x t_net / t_ref. The check must be absolute against this reference. Line-to-line ratios fail, because a sniffer loads SCK, MOSI, CS and DC about equally.
- Timing source: TIM input capture where a channel exists (PA5 = TIM2_CH1, PA7 = TIM3_CH2); PA4 has none and needs DWT polling.
- Deliverable, on at least 5 sealed EVT units with panel and flex fitted (the pq1 bench board has no LCD): intra-unit repeatability, drift over temperature, humidity and flex reseating, inter-unit spread, and the delta from a real probe clip and a soldered MCU-input tap.

Expected numbers (all derived, none measured on pq1):
- R_pu is 30/40/50 kOhm min/typ/max and C_IO is 5 pF typ (STM32U585 datasheet).
- Net capacitance (pad + trace + FPC + NV3007 input) is UNMEASURED; 15-30 pF is assumed.
- That gives tau of roughly 0.6-1.2 us, i.e. about 100-190 core cycles at 160 MHz.
- 1 pF moves the crossing by about 48 ns at 40 kOhm. That is about 8 CPU cycles, or about 8 timer ticks at 6.25 ns.
- Resolution: a polling loop (5-8 cycles per sample) quantises at roughly 0.7-1 pF. Input capture is nominally about 0.13 pF, but the noise floor is UNMEASURED.
- Expected tap load: 3-10 pF for a soldered wire plus an MCU input pin; about 1 pF or less for a FET- or comparator-buffered tap; under 0.5 pF for non-contact pickup.
- Unit-to-unit spread: R_pu alone is +/-25%, which is +/-5 pF equivalent on a 20 pF net, so an uncalibrated design band cannot resolve the tap. With the PA6 reference, the residual is pin-to-pin pull-up mismatch (UNMEASURED) plus FPC/panel lot spread (UNMEASURED) plus temperature drift (UNMEASURED).
- GO criterion: worst-case honest drift plus spread is less than half the smallest soldered-tap delta. Otherwise close the item as an accepted residual with data.

PHASE 1 — only on GO: secure-world self-check, estimated at a few KB.
- Where it runs: the updatable secure image, at boot and immediately before show_mnemonic, enter_pin, the restore wizard and sign. Not the FSBL, for five reasons:
  1. An un-retunable analog threshold inside the WRP + RDP-2-frozen range is permanent (invariant #10).
  2. The FSBL has 4,064 B free (28,704 of 32,768 B) and that is already contested by #540/#758.
  3. It has no I2C or backlight stage (#705).
  4. It runs at HSI16, so timing resolution is 10x coarser.
  5. The threat here is foreign hardware under genuine firmware, so a pre-handoff position buys nothing.
- Baseline: a factory record written at the RDP-0 prodtest stage with the final panel and enclosure fitted, into a one-shot OTP quad-word (176 of 512 B used, secure/src/hw/otp.rs:131-190). It cannot be a flash page: a reseller with SWD at RDP-0 would simply re-measure and rewrite it, and pages 123..=127 must be blank at first boot (secure/src/first_boot/mod.rs:197-205).
- What the buyer can SWD-verify: that the record sits inside a published design/fleet band, and, if the #249 factory manifest lands, that it is signed and UID-bound. The per-unit value itself is not reproducible from the build.
- The design/fleet band is the only layer that can catch an implant present before enrolment, and only if Phase 0 shows the fleet spread is tighter than the tap delta.
- Baseline integrity needs no secret. CMAC_DHUK binding is recomputable by any secure-world code and is irrelevant to a hardware-only adversary.
- On a miss: a loud recoverable "HARDWARE CHANGED" refusal of wizard and sign. No wipe, no TAMP erase, no PIN-budget charge, no halt sink (#835 lesson). Bench and QEMU builds are compiled out.

PHASE 2 — optional, EVT spin only (D-03, narrowed).
- An INA226-class monitor on the main PCB at the USB-C-side VBUS node (USB_VBUS -> ET9555M OVP -> ET83101 buck), read over the existing S-reserved I2C2 aux bus. This avoids an ADC pad, a mask move and a GTZC ADC12 change.
- Calibrated quiescent read with LCM_EN, RGB_EN and LDO2_EN low, normalised to measured VBUS, plus a threshold alert while VBUS is present. Refuse only.
- Expected floor about 2-5 mA against about 25-45 mA quiescent. Both figures are UNMEASURED verifier estimates.
- It catches an awake radio or MCU drawing from the device. It is a cost-raiser, not prevention.

members.note: Round-1 feasibility REFUTED the load-bearing TSC leg, and I honour that: AF9 exists only on PB4-7 and PB12-14, so no display, button or I2C1 net is reachable. Kept: the design-band-plus-enrolled-baseline framing, the refusal-not-wipe sink and the temperature-compensation requirement, now carried by D-02's RC method. Dropped: TSC, the ADC4 AWD to TAMP erase, page-127 storage, the pre-FSBL-window placement, and the claim 'detected unless sub-pF and battery-powered'. Re-rated from L/P1 to research.

Passed all three lenses and is the core of Phase 1, with the round-1 corrections applied: absolute measurement against the PA6 reference pad instead of line-vs-line ratios; OTP (or the #249 signed manifest) instead of a flash page; enrolment under the prodtest image with the final panel and enclosure; panel powered during the measurement; button nets added to scope; input capture where available. Now gated behind the Phase 0 study and re-rated P1 to P2. The mask pad is PA6, not PA5.

Passed all lenses as a hardware cost-raiser. Kept as optional Phase 2 with corrections: INA226 on I2C2 rather than shunt-to-ADC (only PA6 is ADC-capable among the free pads and the mask owns it; a 5 V common-mode shunt needs an amplifier anyway); VBUS-side placement; VBUS normalisation; threshold alert instead of two spot reads. The claim that the shunt 'forces' a visible main-board modification is dropped: the Ledger implant was itself a main-board modification. P1 to P3.

No round-1 verdict; verified here. Confirmed: no ADC/TSC/COMP/OPAMP use anywhere in secure/src or fsbl/src (grep returns nothing), and no Trezor precedent (the trezor-firmware tree has ADC4 only in tamper.c comments at :146/:150/:151 and HAL_TSC commented out in hal_conf.h:86). Refuted: its TSC leg (PA4/PA5/PA7, PA6 and PC13 have no TSC function) and its PDN leg (the consumption-mask stimulus drives an NC pad and loads nothing; the on-chip PDN variant, eprint 2022/946, failed verification in deep_research.json). Kept: 'bench study first, go/no-go on measured drift versus implant delta, never wipe' becomes Phase 0. Its XL/P3 rating was the most honest of the four.

dropped_parts: TSC charge-transfer on display, button or SE nets (IMP-03, BOOT-10): no AF9 on PA0/1/4/5/7, PB0/1/2/8/9; the only reachable SE nets (PB6/PB7) carry 3.3 kOhm pull-ups and would back-power the SEs with the rail off.

ADC4 analog watchdog routed to TAMP confirmed-mode erase (IMP-03): a false trip on a USB-powered supercap device erases the BHK that roots the final SE050 SCP03/admin credentials, bricking the SE050 (see #712). ITAMP7/12/13 are enabled but unfed in both pq1 (secure/src/hw/tamp.rs:199-221) and Trezor.

PDN-response fingerprint via ADC plus the consumption-mask stimulus (BOOT-10, IMP-03): the mask is an unloaded 10 kHz PWM on an NC pad; the literature supports only offline VNA golden-reference methods.

Placing the check or its thresholds in the FSBL or 'before the FSBL fingerprint window' (IMP-03, and the cluster question): frozen forever by WRP + RDP-2, 4,064 B free, no backlight stage (#705), HSI16 clock.

Baseline stored in page 127 or any page 123..=127 (IMP-03, BOOT-10, D-02 'per-device page'): first_boot R2.2 halts on any non-blank page there, page 127 is the journal and salt, and a flash page is rewritable over SWD at RDP-0.

First-boot self-enrolled baseline as the supply-chain defence (IMP-03 b, BOOT-10): it cannot catch an implant present at enrolment. It survives only as a possible later evil-maid layer, and has no free storage page (#601 found the geometry registry full).
Ratiometric line-vs-line detection (D-02): the real sniffer loads all lines about equally.
Shunt read directly by an ADC pad on 'PA10 or PA6' (D-03, IMP-03): PA10, PC13 and PB4 have no ADC channel; PA6 is the production-forced mask; a current-sense amplifier is mandatory.
Rail-current sensing on the LCD rail (IMP-03, BOOT-10 leg 3): backlight current of tens of mA swamps an mW-scale implant, and a competent implant sleeps at uA.
Wasserstein/Frechet distance comparison (BOOT-10): unjustified complexity for a per-net scalar band in a no-heap image.
Detection of an EM or laser FI probe parked over the package (BOOT-10 threat): no measurement mechanism was proposed that reaches it.
CMAC_DHUK or other measurement-bound sealing of the baseline: recomputable by any secure-world code, and unnecessary against a hardware-only adversary.
The claims 'only firmware-reachable mechanism' and 'turns accepted residual into detected' (IMP-03): overclaim; this is a cost-raiser with a floor near 1 pF.
BOOT-10's own already-dropped list (typed FSBL handoff block, genuine LED, CI enrolment holes, #601, glitch campaign): out of this cluster's scope.

#595 (open): per-unit option-byte record in the factory prodtest report. Same prodtest runner and receipt the Phase 0/1 enrolment would extend.
#268 (open): first-boot provisioning and RDP-0 verifiable shipping. The unclosed factory handoff that any factory-enrolled baseline depends on.
#705 (open): the FSBL cannot light the pq1 panel. One reason the check cannot live in the FSBL, and the source of the analog-mode IDR lesson.
#540 / #758 (open): FSBL geometry cutover and 5th-page conflict. The FSBL byte budget is already contested.
#47, #75, #208, #248 (open): TAMP hardware-mode erase, escalation, BHK masking, PVD supervisor. The sink IMP-03 wanted to feed; explicitly not used here.
#220 (open): vendor-pubkey OTP hash region. Competes for the same 512 B OTP and needs one layout owner.
#601 (open): user-personalised boot artifact. Documents that no free flash page exists for per-device data.
#258, #260, #784 (per round-1 verifier, not re-read): content-side display-sniff mitigations (decoy and constant-pixel rendering). Complementary; they detect nothing.
#835 (open): the halt-sink lesson. The refusal path must be recoverable and must not burn PIN budget.
merge.untracked_delta:
Nothing tracks electrical sensing of any net. Issue searches for implant, capacitance, shunt, current sense, ADC, tamper mesh, display bus, logger and enclosure return nothing relevant. Four items are needed:
1. A Phase 0 issue: bench RC-decay characterisation on sealed EVT units with go/no-go criteria (surface:hardware, surface:trusted-ui).
2. An OTP-layout decision for a baseline quad-word, coordinated with #220 and #249.
3. An amendment to docs/security/user-device-verification.md:163-168 once data exists, stating what is and is not detected.
4. An EVT-owner ask for the Phase 2 footprint.
decision_conflicts: docs/security/user-device-verification.md:163-168 records bus loggers as an accepted residual 'as for every wallet vendor'. It is a stated residual, not a prohibition, but the doc must be amended rather than contradicted, and must not be upgraded to 'detected'.
Invariant #10: no runtime writes to the FSBL range and the FSBL is frozen at RDP-2. The check therefore lives in the secure image; the proposals' 'FSBL or similar' placement is rejected.
first_boot R2.2 (secure/src/first_boot/mod.rs:197-205) requires pages 123..=127 blank at first field boot, which conflicts with every flash-page baseline proposal. Resolved by using OTP.

The consumption mask is production-forced on PA6/TIM3_CH1 (secure/src/board/pq1.rs:301-318). Using PA6 as the reference pad needs the mask paused during the roughly millisecond measurement (owner sign-off). The D-03 ADC route would need the mask moved to PB4; the INA226 route avoids that.
Keep-BHK decision and #712: no tamper erase on an analog threshold. The cluster is refuse-only.
#835 halt-sink lesson and 'no new per-signature flash state': the pre-sign check writes nothing and must be a recoverable refusal.
Secure-slot budget: ui-px is 76,949 B over the 466,944 B slot and the non-ui-px image has 34,071 B headroom. A few-KB check is affordable only outside the ui-px overrun, which is an owner lever.
The shipping model (#36/#268) leaves the per-unit factory handoff unapproved. A factory-enrolled baseline inherits that open gate and cannot be claimed before S-1/S-2-class closure.
Invariant #5 (one signing primitive): a signed baseline record must reuse the #249 factory-manifest mechanism, not introduce a new key or algorithm.
hardware_asks: Phase 0 (no board change): at least 5 sealed EVT units with panel and flex fitted, for a thermal, humidity and reseat sweep, plus one sacrificial unit for probe-clip and soldered-tap deltas.

Confirm from the image-only schematic (docs/hardware/schematics/AL_A66_MB_V10_20260826_1500.pdf, no text layer; I did not read it) whether any series resistor, pull or ESD part sits on LCM CS/SCK/MOSI/DC and on the button nets. This changes tau and the method.
Confirm PA6 really is an unrouted pad with no stub, since its validity as the R_pu x C_pad reference depends on it.

Phase 2 (EVT spin): INA226-class footprint with Kelvin shunt at the USB-C-side VBUS node on the main PCB, on I2C2 (PB13/PB14), with the supercap charge path downstream of the shunt. Route the alert line to a free pad that is NOT PC13 (PC13 is TAMP_IN1).
Optional: a guard or ground pour, and no exposed test points, on the LCD and button nets, so that a tap requires a visible rework.
prerequisites: A prodtest image carrying the RC-decay measurement and reporting raw counts into the prodtest receipt (the #595 runner).
A measured GO from Phase 0 before any refusal path is written.
An OTP layout owner decision, coordinated with #220 and #249, and a one-shot encoding (the quad-word is program-once).
Closure or explicit scoping of the factory handoff (#268) for the enrolment step.
A published design/fleet band derived from Phase 0 and production data.
ui-px flash lever decision if the check must ship in a ui-px image.
merge.precedent:
No shipped wallet does electrical (capacitance, impedance or current) self-fingerprinting of any net.
- Trezor, verified in /home/nicola/repos/trezor-firmware at 6ab39e95: core/embed/sec/tamper/stm32u5/tamper.c:140-152 enables ITAMP7/12/13 with "ADC4 analog watchdog" comments but no ADC4 or TSC code exists (HAL_TSC is commented out in hal_conf.h:86). T3W1 has one contact tamper input (TAMPER_INPUT_2, trezor_t3w1_revC.h:326). Capacitance and impedance greps hit only battery, NFC and SD code. Per the round-1 verifier, the npm1300 PMIC measures battery current but nothing security-gates on it.
- Ledger: its response to the Nano X implant was photos, authorised resellers and "further hardening for future products" (Grand slides, per deep_research.json). The tapped bus was SE-driven, so an SE-driven screen does not help.
- Vendor claims not checked by me: Passport Prime tamper pins guarding the display assembly, GridPlus mesh, the bypassed SafePal S1 shield switch.
- Academic: PACTOR (ISSCC 2024, about 0.5 pF, needed a temperature-selected threshold); Kinugawa and Hayashi (EMC Europe 2022, on-chip touch sensor on live traces); PDNPulse (TIFS 2023, offline VNA against a golden reference); Piliposyan (IEEE TC, INA219, reliable only at about 40-50 mW and above; LOF F1 0.88 at 5 mW).
merge.residual_after:
After Phase 1 (if Phase 0 says GO), an attacker can still:
- Use a FET- or comparator-buffered tap (about 1 pF or less) or a non-contact capacitive/EM pickup (under 0.5 pF), both below the floor.
- Trim a tap, or remove compensating capacitance, to stay inside the band's drift margin.
- Swap the panel or flex module with the implant inside it. This re-centres the net, and any fleet band wide enough for lot variation admits it.
- Swap the whole board, or fit a fake MCU that reports a clean measurement. Only #249 UID-bound attestation and the SWD ceremony address that.
- Fit an implant before factory enrolment, or collude with the factory, unless the fleet band is tight enough (unknown until measured).
- Tap nets that are not measured: the SE I2C (encrypted anyway), the USB lines, and the buttons if those prove unmeasurable.
- Use an implant that actively disconnects itself during the roughly millisecond test window (analog switch, about 1 pF off-state). That is costlier but feasible, since the test moments are predictable.
- Flash malicious secure firmware that skips the check. That is the fingerprint and measured-boot story, not this one.

After Phase 2, an attacker can still:
- Use a self-powered implant (coin cell), unless the enclosure leaves no cavity.
- Use an implant that sleeps at uA and transmits when the device is unpowered or from its own storage capacitor.
- Tap between the receptacle and the shunt.
- Tamper with the sense chain itself, as the Ledger implant did with its NTC and fuel gauge.

Net claim allowed: "raises the cost of cheap soldered loggers and awake radios". Not "detects implants".
merge.rationale:
The four members are one idea whose most ambitious form (TSC, PDN, tamper-erase, FSBL placement) is refuted on this package. What survives is a cheap, firmware-only measurement whose physics is sound on these pads but whose signal-to-spread ratio is unknown. Every load-bearing number other than R_pu and C_IO is unmeasured.

So the honest deliverable is a measured go/no-go, not a shipped gate. A gate with an uncharacterised false-positive rate nags or bricks honest units, and a gate that claims more than a roughly 1 pF floor misleads buyers.

Priority is P2 rather than P1 because it is a cost-raiser with enumerated bypasses, it depends on the unclosed factory handoff, and the content-side mitigations (#258/#260/#784: never render secrets in a template-matchable way) address the same attack without a detection floor. It is not a drop: Phase 0 is cheap, it directly answers the owner's question with data, and no vendor has published such data.

The advisor tool was rate-limited and the codex MCP was down, so no external cross-check was run.

skeptic.reason:
The core survives: a bench go/no-go study first, refuse-only, placed in the secure image rather than the FSBL, with no claim of "detects implants". I could not break that shape on bypass, feasibility, tracking or decision grounds. Four things in the recommendation are wrong or incomplete and need fixing before it goes downstream.

**1. The button-net leg is dead (feasibility).** Each pq1 button pad pair is "signal + GND with a 100nF cap and an ESD diode and no board pull-up" (docs/hardware/evt-silicon-validation.md:470-471; secure/src/hw/buttons.rs:96-98). With the 40 kOhm internal pull-up, tau is about 4 ms, so a 5 pF tap changes it by roughly 50 ppm. That is unmeasurable. A button logger also only needs Hz-range bandwidth, so it can hide behind megaohms of series resistance. The title, threat coverage and Phase 1 scope all claim button nets; only the display nets are candidates.

**2. The OTP baseline slot is not free in the planned layout (decision conflict).** "176 of 512 B used" is true today (secure/src/hw/otp.rs:178-190). But the rollback Draft 1.1 candidate provisionally assigns 27 of the 32 quad-words to rollback records and defines a complete 32-entry ownership map (docs/security/a-b-firmware-rollback-architecture.md:1272, :3857, :3926-3931). Adding the master key (2), the sentinel (1) and #220's vendor-key hash (at least 2) leaves nothing. The recommendation names only #220 and #249 as competitors.

**3. The PA6 reference caps the resolution well above the quoted 0.13 pF.** Derived, not measured: PA6 alone is about 5 pF x 40 kOhm = 200 ns, which is about 24-40 timer ticks at 6.25 ns. One tick of error on the reference is 2.5-4%, or about 0.5-0.8 pF on a 20 pF net. The GPIO edge and the timer share one clock, so averaging does not dither this away. PA6 itself is TIM3_CH1, so it can be captured. PA7's capture channel is on TIM3, the mask timer (PSC=0, secure/src/hw/consumption_mask.rs:347-348). The honest floor is about 1 pF on every line, which is the same order as a buffered tap.

**4. Phase 0 has an unlisted blocker.** The bench board has no LCD and no buttons fitted. The sealed EVT units cannot yet run our firmware: no exposed SWD, DFU-only via a BOOT0/SBU bridge (#695, open). Phase 0 is not "firmware only, cheap" until that closes.

**Bypass.** The enumerated residual is honest. Two additions:
- The source and threshold are public, so the adaptive step from the Ledger-style direct-solder implant to one that passes is a low-capacitance buffer front end (my estimate, about 1 pF or less; a few dollars and some analog skill). The cost increase is small.
- The rationale leans on content-side mitigations that are not working today. #258 records that decoy-flicker "FAILS — decoys are visible at every hold" at 20 MHz and `decoy-frames` stays off; #260 is a reconsideration; #784 is an open bypass in the restore wizard.

**Tracking.** All 17 cited issues exist and are open with matching titles. Searches for implant, capacitance, current sense, tamper mesh and SPI sniff return nothing relevant, so "untracked" holds. Missing from the list: #695, and the rollback OTP map.

**Decisions.** No recorded decision prohibits a study. The residual at docs/security/user-device-verification.md:163-168 is a stated boundary, not a ban.

**Not checked.** I did not re-verify the Trezor citations, the datasheet R_pu/C_IO values or the literature claims; none decides the verdict. The advisor was rate-limited and the codex MCP was down, so there was no external cross-check.
skeptic.corrections:
1. Remove button nets (PA0/PA1) from the title, threat coverage, Phase 0 deliverable and Phase 1 scope. The 100 nF cap and ESD diode per pad (evt-silicon-validation.md:470-471) make RC-decay detection impossible there. State button and PIN logging as a fully uncovered residual. The residual line "the buttons if those prove unmeasurable" becomes "buttons are unmeasurable".

2. Rewrite the resolution numbers. The floor is set by the PA6 reference (about 24-40 ticks), giving roughly 0.5-0.8 pF of synchronous quantisation that averaging does not remove. PA4 (DWT polling) is about 1 pF. So the realistic floor is about 1 pF on all lines, not 0.13 pF. Phase 0 must report whether noise dithers the quantisation, and should evaluate two alternatives:
   - per-unit absolute counts with temperature compensation;
   - a known C0G reference capacitor on a free pad. This is a board change and belongs in hardware_asks.

3. Note the timer facts. PA7 capture is TIM3_CH2 and TIM3 is the mask timer (PSC=0), so it can free-run alongside CH1 PWM. PA6 capture is TIM3_CH1 and needs the pad switched from PWM output to input. PB0 (DC) is not given a timing source in the proposal.

4. Add an OTP conflict entry. Rollback Draft 1.1 provisionally claims 27 of 32 quad-words with a full 32-entry ownership map (a-b-firmware-rollback-architecture.md:1272, :3926-3931). Together with master (2), sentinel (1) and #220 this fully subscribes OTP. The baseline needs an explicit quad-word carved out of that map by the owner, or must ride in the #249 signed manifest. If it rides in the manifest, say where the manifest is stored: a flash page reintroduces both the rewrite-at-RDP-0 problem and the pages 123..=127 blank rule.

5. Define behaviour when the baseline quad-word is virgin. Shipping builds must refuse; bench builds are compiled out. Otherwise a factory that skips enrolment silently disables the check.

6. Add #695 (sealed EVT units cannot run our firmware; DFU-only) as a Phase 0 prerequisite and tracked issue. Results must come out over USB prodtest, since sealed units have no SWD. The soldered-tap delta needs an opened unit. Drop the "cheap" framing; Phase 0 alone is cost M and blocked on hardware access.

7. Soften the rationale's reliance on #258/#260/#784. #258 says decoy-flicker fails at 20 MHz and the feature is off; #784 is an open bypass. The content side currently mitigates little, which is an argument for the study, not for deprioritising it.

8. State the bypass cost plainly: the detector is open source, so the adaptive attacker adds a low-capacitance buffer front end. Keep the allowed claim as "raises the cost of direct-soldered loggers on the display nets only".

9. Phase 2: I2C2 already carries the AW99703 backlight driver at 0x36 and the RGB driver (pq1.rs:121, :242), so an address check is needed. A sleeping implant defeats it. Keep at P3 or drop to "EVT-owner question only".

10. Priority. Given open ship blockers S-1/S-2/S-3, #268 and #712, an unknown signal-to-spread ratio and the roughly 1 pF floor, re-rate the cluster to P3 (research; file the Phase 0 issue). Do not write Phase 1 code before a measured GO.

A baseline quad-word conflicts unless the owner carves one out. The recommendation did not flag this.

first_boot R2.2 (secure/src/first_boot/mod.rs:197-205): no baseline in pages 123..=127. The recommendation complies via OTP, subject to the OTP conflict above.
